stem:
Indira watches the roots of a sapling take up water from the soil. Living parts of a habitat are biotic; non-living parts such as water and soil are abiotic.

Which type of habitat interaction is this?

options.text: A biotic–biotic interaction, because the sapling and the water are both treated as living.
A biotic–abiotic interaction, because a living plant interacts with non-living water.
An abiotic–abiotic interaction, because water and soil are both non-living.
No interaction, because the soil and water never meet the plant.

teacher.key_rationale: A living plant taking up non-living water is a biotic–abiotic interaction.
